transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um, so I came in because... well, even when I know I did my safety check on my cab—I drive a taxi, you know? Usually they give me one of the older sedans, but sometimes they put me in this newer hybrid which I actually really hate because the brakes feel totally different. Like, kind of spongy? I don't know if you drive a hybrid, but it takes a lot of getting used to, especially in city traffic. 

But anyway, I do my checks, but this thought just keeps hitting me out of nowhere that I missed something on the cab and somebody is gonna get hurt because of it. Or that my boss will say I lied about doing the inspection. My boss is just... he's on everyone's case lately because dispatch messed up some routes last week, so everyone is on edge. But I just can't make the thought shut up. It's just constantly there while I'm driving. Or even when I'm at home trying to study. I'm trying to finish up my high school diploma online right now, and I'm taking this history class, and the textbook is just so dry. It's like, who even cares about the agricultural revolution, you know? But yeah, I can't focus on it at all because my brain is just stuck on the cab.
Do these thoughts about missing something on the cab feel intrusive and unwanted, and do you try to ignore or suppress them?

Yeah, exactly. They just pop into my head completely uninvited, and I hate it. I try so hard to push them away or just ignore them. Like I said, I'll be sitting there trying to read about, I don't know, crop rotation in the 1700s—which is just as boring as it sounds, by the way. My history teacher, Mr. Davies, he does these video lectures and he has this really monotone voice. It's like listening to a lawnmower from three blocks away. I actually fell asleep during one last week and woke up with my face on the keyboard. 

But yeah, I try to focus on Mr. Davies or the road, but I just can't suppress it. It's like, I know I did the safety check, but the thought just hammers at me that I missed something and someone's gonna get hurt, or my boss is gonna accuse me of lying. I try to block it out, but it just won't shut up, whether I'm driving the cab or trying to study.

When these thoughts come up about missing something on the cab, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking things over and over, counting, or going through specific mental steps—to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah, I... I do. Before I can even take a ride, I have to walk around the car and check everything. The tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork... I just do it over and over. 

Speaking of the tires, though, the roads downtown are just awful right now. There’s this massive pothole on 4th Street that literally swallowed a hubcap off a delivery truck the other day. The city takes forever to fill them, and it messes up the alignment so bad. My buddy Dave—he drives the day shift—he actually popped a tire on it Tuesday and had to wait two hours for a tow. 

But anyway, yeah, I keep checking the car. Sometimes I even take pictures on my phone of the doors and the meter just to prove to myself I looked at them. And the meter, man, it’s this old clunky thing where the receipt paper jams constantly. It jammed when I had this lady going to the airport last month, and she was furious. She had this tiny little dog in her purse that just kept yapping the entire ride, and she wouldn't even let me apologize without rolling her eyes... 

Wait, what was I saying? Right, the checking. If the check doesn't feel exactly right, I have to completely restart the whole routine from the beginning. I'll just keep going around the car. I do it even if I'm already late and the passengers are literally standing right there on the curb waiting for me, just staring at me while I walk in circles taking pictures of the headlights. I just can't drive off until it feels right.
When you have these intrusive thoughts about missing something on the cab, do you feel anxious or distressed, and does that feeling lead you to check things repeatedly?

Yeah, I mean, the anxiety is just... it's overwhelming. It feels like this tight knot in my chest, and the only way to make it even a little bit better is to do the checking. So yeah, before I can take a ride, I just keep going around the car. Tires, lights, doors, meter, paperwork... over and over. 

And the paperwork, honestly, is a nightmare anyway. The taxi commission just updated all their forms last month, and they printed them on this weird glossy paper that smears if you use a gel pen. I love gel pens—I buy those multi-packs with the different colors because they write so smooth, you know? But now I have to use these cheap ballpoint pens that always skip. I bought a pack at the drugstore on 8th Avenue, and the guy behind the counter was so rude. He just threw my change on the counter. I hate when people do that instead of handing it to you. 

But anyway, yeah, the distress is so bad that I'll take pictures of the car parts on my phone, and if the whole routine doesn't feel exactly right, I have to restart the entire check from scratch. I'll just keep doing it, even if I'm already super late and the passengers are literally standing right there on the curb, just staring at me while I walk in circles. I just can't stop until the anxiety goes down.
